header:
Date: 2026-08-10
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan Walker (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Bluefin Lead ML Eng), Tom Nguyen (Bluefin Platform Eng), Asha Patel (Bluefin SRE)
summary: Demo/walkthrough focused on how Redwood handles very long context windows (deep conversation/history), sustained high TPS bursts, and streaming backpressure/timeouts. Covered runtime behaviors, KV cache eviction, graceful fallbacks to shorter variants, and suggested pilot steps.
topics: KV cache eviction and prefix caching
Fallbacks: model variants, regional routing, canary + rollbacks
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Walker: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, then we will jump into a live console walkthrough.
[00:08] Sofia Ramirez: Hi, Sofia here. excited. we have a big holiday peak coming so we want to understand worst case.
[00:12] Tom Nguyen: Tom, platform. our main concern is sustained 12k qps burst across multiple endpoints and how streaming behaves under pressure.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Maya from Redwood, I will demo console and the Optimize suggestions, and run a short stress sequence from our sandbox.
[00:28] Asha Patel: Asha, SRE; also curious about network egress and how private deployments behave.
[00:35] Ethan Walker: Great. quick agenda: 1) long-history behavior, 2) high TPS & backpressure, 3) demo fallbacks & rollouts, 4) next steps. we'll reference the perf spreadsheet I uploaded (link in chat).
[00:46] Sofia Ramirez: got it. and security doc?
[00:48] Ethan Walker: yes I'll share SOC2 and network diagram after.
[00:50] [00:50] --- Demo start ---
[01:02] Maya Chen: ok I'm in the Redwood Console. first thing, long context. Bluefin's use case is long user sessions where we keep 20+ turns of chat and a product catalog blob of ~40k tokens. so we showed a simplified prompt here.
[01:18] Sofia Ramirez: yeah, our embedding cache and historical context is super important, we can't truncate previous offers.
[01:25] Maya Chen: the runtime uses prefix/K-V cache so repeated prefixes don't re-execute full attention. note: sometimes the transcription may say K V but our docs show KV cache. there's also an LRU eviction policy per session, and we have heuristics to keep recent turns.
[01:41] Tom Nguyen: how does that behave under spike? e.g., if 12k qps for 3 minutes, does the cache thrash and cause latency spikes?
[01:50] Maya Chen: good question. in Dedicated or Private, you can reserve larger KV capacity. on Hosted we do a best-effort with adaptive eviction. when eviction rate jumps we start continuous batching fallbacks and prefer shorter model variants.
[02:06] Sofia Ramirez: can you show the console metrics for a synthetic spike?
[02:10] Maya Chen: sure. I'm switching to the Dashboard -> Model routes. you'll see a simulated surge run here (note: we used our edge stress harness).
[02:18] [02:18] Maya Chen: alright the first graph is tokens/s and you can see batch sizes consolidate, there's a small latency tail at minute 2.
[02:28] Ethan Walker: two important knobs: batching window and history window. you can set a per-route max_history_tokens to control how much of the past gets sent; Optimize can recommend a quantized history knob based on measured latency cost.
[02:42] Tom Nguyen: if we reduce history to 8k tokens, do we lose relevant context? our metric is product recall in the last 5 turns.
[02:50] Maya Chen: that's where cached embeddings and reranking come in. you can offload the large catalog to embeddings and only include sparse contextual pointers in the prompt. Optimize will recommend a hybrid approach.
[03:02] Sofia Ramirez: show the fallbacks: when a request times out or exceeds streaming window what happens?
[03:08] Maya Chen: demo time. I'm going to launch a streaming session and then inject CPU/GPU contention in the sandbox.
[03:15] [03:15] Maya Chen: starting stream now. (typing noises) you'll see partial tokens come in. note: streaming uses chunked flushes at the runtime, with a per-chunk timeout.
[03:30] [03:30] Maya Chen: injecting contention — okay now the stream is delayed, client sees delayed chunks and a keepalive is sent. if the chunk timeout elapses the runtime triggers our fallback policy: 1) try model variant with lower memory (quantized), 2) if still constrained, route to a compatible regional pool, 3) finally return a short stub response and mark session for retry.
[03:56] Asha Patel: is the stub response configurable, like include a machine-readable reason code?
[04:00] Maya Chen: yes, you can configure structured fallback payloads and a header that indicates fallback_reason: kvcache_eviction | timeout | overload. we also log token-level cost so you can debug later.
[04:14] Tom Nguyen: regarding retries, how do you prevent thundering herd on fallback? if 12k clients all retry suddenly we get another surge.
[04:24] Ethan Walker: we advise exponential backoff + jitter at client. Redwood Console can also coordinate a gradual fallback ramp: you can set a canary ratio and a circuit-breaker window so only X% of retries hit the fallback target.
[04:40] Sofia Ramirez: can you show the Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization?
[04:45] Maya Chen: switching to Optimize tab. here we have a suggestion: for your arg pattern (short instruction, long history) it recommends per-model quantization profile q4_0 for gpt-like open models and batching window 30ms at 2k qps, 50ms for peak 12k. we show estimated cost delta too.
[05:04] Tom Nguyen: those ms numbers seem tight — how do you measure them in the field?
[05:08] Maya Chen: we use tail-latency probes and token-level instrumentation; the Console shows p50/p95/p99 token latency and predicted cost per million tokens. note sometimes the auto transcription of these labels in the export is messy, e.g. p99 becomes p nine nine in some exports.
[05:22] [05:22] Ethan Walker: quick pause — any blockers to trying a pilot?
[05:26] Sofia Ramirez: security signoff is needed, we are reviewing SOC2 and want to confirm BYOK/KMS options.
[05:31] Ethan Walker: yes, for Private (VPC/on-prem) we support customer-managed KMS; for Hosted we have envelope encryption and HSM options in Dedicated. I'll drop the SOC2 link.
[05:43] Asha Patel: what about audit logs retention and RBAC?
[05:46] Maya Chen: Console -> Security shows per-route audit events, and you can configure retention up to 7 years for Dedicated/private. RBAC integrates with SAML/SSO; we map roles to route-level permissions.
[05:58] Tom Nguyen: back to streaming — what happens to the KV cache when we switch to quantized variant? shouldn't quantization change tokenization offsets?
[06:06] Maya Chen: good technical spot. our runtime keeps abstracted KV keys by logical turn, so quantization is an execution path; the KV references remain stable. occasionally embeddings change slightly post-quant which can cause minor rerank noise but we've seen sub-percent differences in our benchmarks.
[06:23] Sofia Ramirez: can you run a targeted stress with long history retained per session?
[06:27] Maya Chen: launching a test — I'm spinning up 1k concurrent sessions each with 20-turn history and pinging at burst 6k qps then ramping to 12k for 3 minutes.
[06:42] [06:42] Maya Chen: first minute is stable, at minute 2 we see eviction rate climb, at 2:17 a handful of sessions hit chunk timeout and were routed to quantized variant. latency p95 jumps but p99 stays within SLO for 90% of sessions.
[06:58] Tom Nguyen: what was the memory footprint per session in that run?
[07:02] Maya Chen: in this sandbox, ~3.6MB per session for KV around 8k tokens; can vary by model. Dedicated with larger KV heaps reduces eviction frequency.
[07:12] Sofia Ramirez: do you have guidance for session sharding across pods to balance KV memory?
[07:16] Maya Chen: yes, sharding by customer_id or session hash with session affinity helps. Redwood has automatic session placement and you can set session affinity TTL.
[07:26] Asha Patel: our network team worries about egress from Hosted; can we estimate egress costs and peering needs?
[07:32] Ethan Walker: we'll include an egress estimate in the perf spreadsheet; for Private we avoid egress beyond your network.
[07:39] Sofia Ramirez: later in the hour can we deep-dive on the streaming keepalive protocol? we've seen clients disconnect at 30s.
[07:45] Maya Chen: yes, quick overview: runtime emits keepalives at ~15s intervals during idle streaming windows; client should maintain read socket. if client disconnects we mark session as paused and preserve KV for X minutes (configurable session TTL).
[08:02] [08:02] Sofia Ramirez: what about tokenization mismatches across model variants causing alignment issues mid-stream?
[08:08] Maya Chen: runtime uses an interop layer; when switching variants we rebase the KV with a lightweight translation step, sometimes text offsets shift by a token. we log that to help debugging.
[08:22] Tom Nguyen: any historical incidents you can call out? we like real-world examples.
[08:27] Ethan Walker: one retail customer had a Black Friday peak where heavy catalog embeds plus long histories caused cache thrash; we introduced a hybrid approach—move catalog to embedding store and use a summarizer step to keep history small. this reduced p99 by ~40%.
[08:45] Sofia Ramirez: that sounds promising. can we see a step-by-step playbook?
[08:49] Maya Chen: I'll share a short playbook doc — it outlines detection (eviction > 2% for 30s), immediate mitigations (shorten history to 4k, enable fallback -> quantized variant), and medium-term (move catalog to embeddings + reranker). link: https://redwood.example/bluefin-playbook (placeholder).
[09:06] [09:06] Asha Patel: for retries, is the client library opinionated or do we implement our own backoff?
[09:11] Ethan Walker: Redwood SDKs include a recommended retry policy with jitter and adaptive backoff that reads the fallback_reason header. you can also plug your own transport layer.
[09:22] Tom Nguyen: do your SDKs support streaming reconnect and resume mid-chunk? we've had clients that want resumable streams.
[09:29] Maya Chen: not resumable mid-chunk today; we recommend idempotent request ids and resume semantics at chunk boundaries. resumable mid-chunk is on the roadmap but complicated across variants.
[09:45] Sofia Ramirez: show the logs for one session that fell back — we want the exact headers and timeline.
[09:49] Maya Chen: pulling logs... here's an example: session_id=bf-3482, t=00:02:17 chunk_timeout -> fallback_reason=timeout -> route=quantized-v1 -> response_stubs_sent=true -> metric: latency p95=420ms. I will export and attach the raw log to the folder.
[10:09] Ethan Walker: note: the export may have transcription issues; file names sometimes get mangled in the auto export.
[10:14] [10:14] Sofia Ramirez: security again: where do you store these session logs? are they in plaintext?
[10:18] Maya Chen: logs are encrypted at rest; sensitive fields can be redacted by config. Dedicated/private allows you to route logs to your SIEM.
[10:27] Tom Nguyen: let's talk throughput throttles — if qps crosses rate limit, do you queue or reject? how is backpressure signalled to the client?
[10:35] Ethan Walker: Redwood supports both modes. You can set a per-route queuing window; small queue + reject with Retry-After is preferred to avoid large latencies. Backpressure headers include X-Redwood-Queue and X-Redwood-Estimated-Wait. We also expose a streaming-level signal when queueing exceeds threshold.
[10:51] Asha Patel: if we set a tight queue and lots of retries, it might produce retry storms — again client backoff required.
[10:57] Maya Chen: exactly. Console can enforce a circuit-breaker that returns a 503 with a structured body to a fraction of requests to reduce storm pressure.
[11:08] Sofia Ramirez: can Optimize suggest queue sizes?
[11:11] Maya Chen: yes, Optimize forecasts queue behavior from simulated traffic patterns and suggests a reasonable queue window plus a max retry limit.
[11:20] [11:20] Maya Chen: quick demo of Canary deploy for fallbacks: I'm deploying a new routing policy that says 20% of traffic goes to fallback path first, then ramp to 100% if errors drop.
[11:32] Tom Nguyen: how do you measure canary impact for stream sessions?
[11:35] Maya Chen: we trace tokens and session outcomes; the Console overlays canary vs baseline and shows delta on p50/p95/p99 and success rate.
[11:47] Sofia Ramirez: you mentioned regional routing as a mitigation — if one region is overloaded, you'd route to another. but that causes tail latency due to cross-region RTT; thoughts?
[11:58] Ethan Walker: tradeoff: routing to a healthy region reduces failures but increases RTT. We recommend pairing regional fallback with a short stub-first approach: return a short answer immediately, then send full result asynchronously if critical.
[12:13] Tom Nguyen: do you support async callbacks/webhooks for heavy responses?
[12:16] Maya Chen: yes, there is an async mode where you can receive a 202 and webhook later. good for heavy rerank jobs.
[12:24] Sofia Ramirez: in our case we sometimes need a full answer synchronously for checkout flows. what's the recommended SLO?
[12:30] Ethan Walker: for sync-critical flows keep a reserved Dedicated pool with burst capacity; for less critical flows use async with user-visible fallback messages.
[12:40] Asha Patel: what's the typical failover time when switching variants? we care about user-visible pauses.
[12:46] Maya Chen: variant switch is sub-second for routing; chunk timeouts can cause 1-2s visible pause if client waits. the more common better UX is to send a short stub immediately with a progress token and stream full results when ready.
[12:58] [12:58] Sofia Ramirez: any tips for token-level cost savings without hurting recall?
[13:03] Maya Chen: use templated prompts, sparse pointers, reranker + embeddings; also consider compressive summarization of session history. Optimize will profile prompt token contribution to cost and suggest trims.
[13:18] Tom Nguyen: can we do a quick run of a pilot config? like Dedicated small pool + on-hosted fallback region?
[13:24] Ethan Walker: yes I can sketch a pilot config now. we'll propose a Dedicated dev pool with 2 nodes sized for your p99 target, enable regional fallback to us-east, and an Optimize config that recommends batching/quant.
[13:36] Maya Chen: I'm creating a draft config and will attach it. in chat: link to draft pilot config (redwood://configs/bluefin-pilot).
[13:46] Sofia Ramirez: perfect. regarding telemetry, can we stream raw token events into our observability (Datadog)?
[13:52] Maya Chen: yes we have an integration that emits summarized token metrics and you can forward raw traces into your APM in Dedicated/private. Hosted is more constrained but supports exported metrics.
[14:05] Tom Nguyen: one last technical question — does Redwood keep cold/warm model weights across variants for fast warmup or do you pay startup cost when switching?
[14:13] Maya Chen: we keep hot weights for commonly used variants; switching to a rare variant can incur a warmup penalty. Optimize suggests pre-warming if you anticipate fallback.
[14:26] [14:26] Ethan Walker: we're approaching the last 10 minutes. quick recap and confirm next steps.
[14:33] Sofia Ramirez: recap please.
[14:35] Ethan Walker: recap: 1) We demonstrated long-history handling and KV eviction behavior. 2) Showed streaming backpressure, chunk timeouts and fallback policy chain (quantize -> regional route -> stub). 3) Reviewed Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization. 4) Pilot proposed: Dedicated dev pool + fallback routing + telemetry forwarding.
[14:53] Sofia Ramirez: sounds good. we want the perf spreadsheets and the playbook.
[14:57] Ethan Walker: action items in chat. I'll share SOC2 + network diagram + perf. Maya will share playbook and runbook.
[15:06] Tom Nguyen: we'll send sample prompts and traffic profile by Friday.
[15:10] Asha Patel: and we'll schedule the pilot kickoff for week of Aug 17 — need to confirm internal ops.
[15:16] Ethan Walker: great. any final questions?
[15:20] Sofia Ramirez: none from me, thanks.
[15:22] Ethan Walker: thanks all. I'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifact links.
[15:29] [15:29] --- End of call transcript export ---

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mislabels (e.g., "K-V cache" vs "KV cache", "p nine nine" etc.). Shared artifacts: perf spreadsheet (attached in chat), draft pilot config (redwood://configs/bluefin-pilot), playbook link (https://redwood.example/bluefin-playbook).
questions: How does Redwood handle KV cache thrash under sustained 12k qps?
What are the streaming fallback steps and how configurable are they?
Can we run a Dedicated pilot with reserved KV capacity and telemetry forwarding?
